text:
infra-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT: GPU queue spike on private cluster 'cust-edge-42' (region: eu-west-2). Pending inference requests: 86, avg queue wait 52s, autoscaler reported errors adding nodes. Paging @sre-oncall

sre-oncall: ACK — jumping in. grabbing logs + checking autoscaler status. tagging infra team.

devina: i'm seeing a bunch of `NodeProvisionTimeout` in the autoscaler logs, looks like imagepulls are slow and the kubelet is hitting backoff. suspect customer AMI constraints + their private subnet hitting IP exhaustion.

marcus: noted. customer reported recently they tightened their security group rules for worker bootstrap. could block our bootstrap agent. @anya can you confirm the bootstrap connectivity checks?

anya: running connectivity probe now: `curl -sS http://10.10.5.2:8080/health || true` from jump host — failing intermittently. Also DNS lookups for the registry are ~600ms.

sre-oncall: pasting relevant autoscaler fragment:```text
2026-03-15T07:14:22Z autoscaler ERROR scale_up: failed to create node: LaunchTemplateError: subnet has no available IP addresses
2026-03-15T07:14:22Z autoscaler WARN retrying scale_up in 30s (attempt 3)
2026-03-15T07:15:02Z autoscaler ERROR bootstrapping: imagepull timeout after 2m
```

devina: so two distinct failure modes: (1) can't allocate ENIs/IPs in that private subnet, (2) even when nodes start, imagepulls time out because registry access is flaky. both cause the autoscaler to back off -> queue growth.

marcus: mitigation path A (fast): increase routing to fallback hosted registry mirror and temporarily bump `maxNodes` in the autoscaler policy for this cluster. but if subnet has no IPs, new nodes won't get addresses.

anya: i've triggered a manual scale attempt `kubectl scale --replicas=0...` (toy command) — it fails with same launch error.

sre-oncall: calling customer success to confirm changes on their VPC side. @cs-maya can you confirm if they made SG/route changes?

cs-maya: pinged customer in support ticket #CS-2291. customer confirms they applied a host-level deny rule for outbound 443 for the bootstrap agent (policy applied yesterday at 03:00 UTC). they say it was to tighten egress for regulatory reasons.

marcus: ok that explains imagepull failures. for IP exhaustion we need them to free up ENI capacity or add a secondary CIDR to their subnet. asked cs to request a CIDR increase with cloud admin.

devina: short-term workaround: route traffic for registry -> our regional mirror via the cluster's NAT gateway (if available) or use an init container with registry cache image already present to avoid pulling during bootstrap. can push a canary AMI with image baked in but that takes ~45m to bake + validate.

anya: i can flip a temporary routing override on the jump host to tunnel registry traffic via the NAT, but will need customer OK.

sre-oncall: ACTIONS: 1) cs-maya to get customer confirmation for NAT/routing change (in progress). 2) devina to prepare a baked AMI and bake pipeline (ETA 50m). 3) anya to attempt ephemeral registry tunnel (ETA 10m). 4) marcus to hold escalation with infra leads and cloud admin for subnet CIDR increase.

ryan: i'm on standby for handoff at 08:00 UTC. if you're still paged, i'll take over the war room.

sre-oncall: quick customer impact note for the handoff: ~120 affected requests over last 30m, tail latency spikes to 6s (was 200-300ms normally), some customers experiencing failed inferences (HTTP 503). no data plane compromise — only availability/latency.

cs-maya: updated the ticket and emailed the customer's infra lead with exact error snippets and suggested NAT change. they acknowledged and said they'll try temporary NAT route in 8-12 minutes.

devina: starting AMI bake now: `packer build -var 'region=eu-west-2' bake-gpu-base.pkr.hcl` — attaching console link: https://ci.internal/pipelines/5423/logs

anya: registry tunnel established via jump host, doing a new scale test now: `aws autoscaling start-instance-refresh --auto-scaling-group-name ...`

infra-bot: Monitor update: after tunnel, 7 new nodes progressed to Ready; queue dropped from 86 -> 34 within 6 minutes. autoscaler still backing off on further adds due to subnet IP errors.

sre-oncall: good partial recovery. keeping this thread open until NAT route + CIDR fix. handoff to @ryan in 20m if not resolved. capture followups: bake AMI PR, request CIDR increase, add registry mirror to bootstrap docs. :thumbsup:

ryan: I'll take it from 08:00 UTC if still open. please DM me the bake link and ticket id.

cs-maya: Ticket: CS-2291, cloud request created CR-8810 for secondary CIDR. sharing updates in ticket.

sre-oncall: thanks all — closing pager for now, will reopen if queue grows >50 again. ongoing notes appended to the incident runbook.

anya: FYI we should add a healthcheck step to the cluster bootstrap that tests registry reachability and falls back to baked AMI early to avoid slow rollouts. filing a follow-up RFC.

marcus: agreed. logging a post-incident action item: PIA-2890 (bootstrap resilience), assigned to devina + anya.

infra-bot: :white_check_mark: INCIDENT STATUS: partial mitigation applied, customer action pending, on-call handoff scheduled.
